local_context.value: Charleston has a humid subtropical climate; average annual relative humidity is about 72.7% (78.9% in August); "Hurricanes are a major threat to the area during the summer and early fall" (Hurricane Hugo, Category 4, September 21, 1989). City elevation is 3 ft. 15.9% of residents were 65 or older in the 2020 census. 77,479 dwelling units (12.7% vacant). Historic stock: the Pink House, 17 Chalmers Street, built 1694-1712, "is the oldest stone building in Charleston".

neighborhoods.value: City districts named in the article: Downtown/The Peninsula, West Ashley, Johns Island, James Island, Cainhoy Peninsula, Daniel Island (6 districts; no finer neighborhood list found in an official source)

place_entities.value: Medical University of South Carolina Medical Center; Roper Hospital; Ralph H. Johnson VA Medical Center; Arthur Ravenel Jr. Bridge (opened July 16, 2005, links downtown Charleston with Mount Pleasant). Also named: Waterfront Park, The Battery, City Market, Rainbow Row, Fort Sumter National Monument.

permit_office.value: City of Charleston Permit Center (2 George Street, Ground Floor, Charleston, SC 29401; 843-577-5550; permits@charleston-sc.gov) handles building permits inside City limits; permits and inspections via the City's Customer Self Service portal. Charleston County Building Inspection Services is the separate office for unincorporated areas.
